statement: A pineapple and 3 lemons balance 12 lemons. The pineapple also balances 3 oranges. All the lemons weigh the same, and so do all the oranges. How many lemons balance 2 oranges?

choices.misconception: I found how many lemons balance one orange and stopped there.
I forgot the 3 lemons beside the pineapple, so I thought the pineapple balances 12 lemons.
I found how many lemons balance the pineapple and gave that as the answer.
I added the 3 lemons to the 12 instead of taking them away, so I thought the pineapple balances 15 lemons.

hints: Take the same thing off both sides of the first balance.
Balance puzzles: remove equal amounts from both pans to find the pineapple in lemons, then use the second balance to swap the pineapple for oranges.
Taking 3 lemons off each side shows that the pineapple balances 9 lemons.

solutions.reliable: Take 3 lemons off both pans of the first balance: the pineapple balances 12 - 3 = 9 lemons. The pineapple also balances 3 oranges, so 3 oranges balance 9 lemons and one orange balances 9 / 3 = 3 lemons. Two oranges balance 2 x 3 = 6 lemons. The transferable idea: a balance stays level when you remove the same thing from both sides, which lets you write one object in terms of another.
solutions.elegant: Two oranges are two thirds of 3 oranges, so they weigh two thirds of the pineapple, which is two thirds of 9 lemons: 6 lemons.

whyOnTest: Removing equal amounts from both pans, then swapping one object for another, is the whole logic of balance puzzles.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
